data.narrative: Student completed Module 2 CI/CD Pipeline: designed GitHub Actions workflow with sequential stages (lint-test → build → push), implemented security controls (no hardcoded secrets, branch filtering), and added operational hardening (dependency caching, 15-min timeout, image size guardrail). Proactively identified and prevented all three BREAK scenarios (secret exposure, cache poisoning, unintended deployments) through correct design patterns. Demonstrated understanding of pipeline safety and traceability.

dimension_scores.observation: Student leveraged Module 1 Dockerfile in CI/CD pipeline, configured Docker Buildx for efficient builds, and implemented image size validation (200MB threshold).
dimension_scores.evidence: Pipeline uses Dockerfile from Module 1, docker/build-push-action@v5 for multi-stage builds, docker image inspect to check size with explicit fail-if-exceeds-200MB logic.

dimension_scores.observation: Student designed production-ready pipeline with proper stage separation, dependency gating, secret management, and branch filtering. Sequential shape chosen appropriately for project scale.
dimension_scores.evidence: Two explicit jobs with needs: keyword (lint-and-test independent, build-and-push depends on it), if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' blocks non-main pushes, uses GitHub secrets not hardcoded credentials.

dimension_scores.observation: Pipeline includes basic visibility: logs image details on success, 15-min timeout prevents hangs, step names clearly indicate purpose. Deeper observability (metrics, alerts) deferred to Module 4.
dimension_scores.evidence: Step logs image registry/tag/SHA for confirmation, timeout-minutes: 15 prevents resource waste, clear step naming (Lint and Test, Build, Push).

dimension_scores.observation: Student anticipated three specific failure modes (secret leaks, cache breaks, unintended deployments) and built prevention into design rather than recovering after. Failure-First Drill scenarios understood.
dimension_scores.evidence: Pipeline prevents secret exposure (no hardcoded tokens), cache poisoning (cache: pip with requirements.txt key), and unintended deployments (if: condition). Identified all three BREAK scenarios independently.

dimension_scores.observation: Degradation design not yet in scope; pipeline assumes success path. Circuit breakers and graceful fallback patterns defer to Modules 5-6.
dimension_scores.evidence: Pipeline has no fallback paths (no retry logic, no partial success handling). Scope is binary: pass or fail each stage. Appropriate for CI stage; production resilience covered later.

dimension_scores.observation: Student created detailed MODULE2_CI_CD_PIPELINE.md with workflow structure, testing scenarios, tagging strategy, and known limitations. On-call engineer could follow pipeline flow.
dimension_scores.evidence: Documentation includes: four chunks structure, job dependencies, secret management approach, image tagging strategy, failure scenarios (lint break, test break, size breach), registry path, and next steps.

strengths: Proactive security: designed pipeline with secret protection from start (no hardcoded credentials, uses GitHub token masking). Did not need hints on this critical issue.
Pipeline discipline: understood stage separation principle; gated build on test success via needs: keyword. Recognizes that broken tests must stop downstream.
Branch safety: implemented if: condition to prevent feature branches from polluting registry. Understood deployment safety as first-class concern.
Performance awareness: configured dependency caching (cache: pip with requirements.txt key), understood that slow pipelines encourage risky batched commits.
Traceability thinking: chose git SHA tagging over latest tag; explained: 'tells you exactly which commit built this image' for production debugging.
data.recommendation: In Module 3 (Environment Management), extend this CI/CD pipeline to deploy to different environments (dev/staging/prod) with environment-specific configs (.env files, database connections). This connects pipeline-built images to actual running services. Also plan to add pre-commit hooks to catch lint/test issues before pushing to main, creating a fast feedback loop at developer's machine before CI runs.

public_evidence.student_action: Designed and implemented production-ready GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline with four integrated chunks: lint-test, docker-build, image-size-check, registry-push.
public_evidence.technical_detail: Two jobs: lint-and-test (independent, sequential stages), build-and-push (depends on lint-and-test, gated on main branch). Uses docker/build-push-action, dependency caching, GitHub secrets, image size validation.
public_evidence.proof: .github/workflows/ci.yml (110+ lines) with proper YAML structure, job dependencies via needs:, secret masking, if: branch condition, timeout: 15min, cache: pip configuration.
public_evidence.ability: Designs CI/CD pipelines with security, performance, and safety hardening as first-class concerns, not afterthoughts.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows mastery of pipeline anti-patterns (secret leaks, cache misses, unintended deployments) and how to prevent them. Demonstrates that CI/CD is about automation + discipline, not just orchestration.

public_evidence.student_action: Created comprehensive pipeline documentation with workflow structure, design decisions, testing scenarios, and operational guidance.
public_evidence.technical_detail: Documents: trigger config (push to main + PRs), job structure (lint-test independent, build-push dependent), secret management (GitHub token), tagging strategy (SHA immutable + latest mutable), concurrency handling, performance analysis.
public_evidence.proof: Documentation includes: pipeline structure breakdown, failure scenarios with expected outcomes, image tagging rationale, registry path, known limitation (Docker daemon verification deferred).
public_evidence.ability: Communicates pipeline design clearly enough that on-call engineers can understand flow, debug failures, and maintain the system.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows that pipeline thinking extends beyond writing the YAML—includes operational documentation, failure scenarios, and team communication.

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Explained: 'CI is quality check (lint/test run automatically), CD is conveyor belt (push image to registry)' - separated concerns correctly.
Used needs: keyword to gate build on test success; explained: 'if test fails, build doesn't run' - demonstrates pipeline as series of gates.
Used GitHub secrets (GITHUB_TOKEN) instead of hardcoded credentials; understood: 'git history is permanent, secret leaks are impossible to fully revoke.'
Tagged images with github.sha instead of latest; explained: 'tells you exactly which commit built this image' for production debugging.
Configured cache: pip with requirements.txt as key; understood: 'cache miss if lockfile changes, but reuse on subsequent runs.'

teaching_approaches.detail: BREAK scenario with hardcoded secret echoed to logs made secret management tangible. Student proactively prevented it.
Failure-First Drill (break a test, watch pipeline stop before build) made gating logic concrete.

learning_style_signals: Learns well from anti-patterns and failure modes (BREAK scenario recognition)
Connects previous learning to new module (Dockerfile from Module 1 integrated into pipeline)
Reasons about business impact (pipeline speed → batch size → risk trade-off)
